outroLine: How many did you get? Comment your score below, and subscribe with the bell on for a new quiz every day!

lines.q: Thirty questions about our solar system, from easy to legend, and they get harder every round. Keep score! First one: What is the name of our galaxy?
lines.a: The Milky Way! Home to hundreds of billions of stars.

lines.q: How many planets are in our solar system?
lines.a: Eight! Four rocky ones, and four giants.

lines.q: Which planet is third from the Sun?
lines.a: Earth! The only place we know of with life. Nice start!

lines.q: What causes day and night?
lines.a: Earth spinning! One full turn takes about twenty four hours.

lines.q: How long does Earth take to orbit the Sun?
lines.a: About three hundred sixty five days! The extra quarter day gives us leap years.

lines.q: Last one of round one. Which planet is called the Morning Star?
lines.a: Venus! It's the brightest planet in our sky.

lines.q: Round two: medium. Here we go! Which planet has a giant hexagon shaped storm at its north pole?
lines.a: Saturn! Each side of that hexagon is wider than our whole planet.

lines.q: Which planet is farthest from the Sun?
lines.a: Neptune! Pluto goes farther, but it's not a planet anymore.

lines.q: Where is the main asteroid belt?
lines.a: Between Mars and Jupiter! And it's mostly empty space, not a wall of rocks.

lines.q: What is the tallest volcano in the solar system?
lines.a: Olympus Mons, on Mars! About two and a half times as tall as Everest. You're flying!

lines.q: What is Saturn's largest moon?
lines.a: Titan! The only moon with a thick atmosphere.

lines.q: Which planet has a day closest in length to ours?
lines.a: Mars! A Martian day lasts about twenty four hours and thirty seven minutes.

lines.q: Round three: hard. Stay sharp! Which planet is the coldest?
lines.a: Uranus! Not Neptune, even though Neptune is farther out.

lines.q: In which year did Pluto become a dwarf planet?
lines.a: Two thousand six! It had been called a planet for seventy six years.

lines.q: Which planet was predicted with maths before anyone saw it?
lines.a: Neptune! Spotted in eighteen forty six, right where the maths said. If you're enjoying this, subscribe and turn on the bell!

lines.q: What is the largest object in the asteroid belt?
lines.a: Ceres! It's so big it counts as a dwarf planet. Great going so far!

lines.q: Which moon is the most volcanic place we know?
lines.a: Io! This moon of Jupiter has hundreds of active volcanoes.

lines.q: How many people have walked on the Moon?
lines.a: Twelve! All of them on six Apollo missions.

lines.q: Round four: very hard. Only the best get these. How long is one year on Neptune?
lines.a: About one hundred sixty five Earth years! Since we found it, it has only gone round once.

lines.q: What are the names of Mars's two moons?
lines.a: Phobos and Deimos! Their names mean fear and dread. Still with me?

lines.q: Roughly how hot is the surface of the Sun?
lines.a: About five thousand five hundred degrees Celsius! Yet its outer corona tops a million degrees.

lines.q: Which spacecraft is the farthest human made object?
lines.a: Voyager one! Launched in nineteen seventy seven, now beyond the Sun's bubble.

lines.q: Europa, a moon with a hidden ocean, orbits which planet?
lines.a: Jupiter! That ocean may hold more water than all of Earth's seas.

lines.q: How old is our solar system?
lines.a: About four point six billion years! One round left, you've got this!

lines.q: Final round: legend level. Good luck! What is the icy shell at the very edge of our solar system called?
lines.a: The Oort Cloud! Nobody has seen it directly, but comets give it away.

lines.q: Which spacecraft flew past Pluto in twenty fifteen?
lines.a: New Horizons! It found a giant heart shaped plain on Pluto.

lines.q: Titan has lakes, but what are they filled with?
lines.a: Liquid methane! It even rains methane there. Three left, stay with me!

lines.q: How many Earth days is one year on Mercury?
lines.a: Eighty eight days! No planet races round the Sun faster.

lines.q: Who discovered Jupiter's four biggest moons?
lines.a: Galileo Galilei! In sixteen ten, with a telescope he built himself.

lines.q: Final question. Which planet has the most volcanoes?
lines.a: Venus! Scientists have mapped about eighty five thousand of them.

questions.q: What is the name of our **galaxy**?
questions.fact: The Milky Way is about 100,000 light-years across.

questions.q: How many **planets** are in our solar system?
questions.fact: Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars are the four rocky planets.

questions.q: Which planet is **third** from the Sun?
questions.fact: Earth is about 150 million km from the Sun.

questions.q: What causes **day and night**?
questions.fact: At the equator, Earth spins at about 1,670 km/h.

questions.q: How long does Earth take to **orbit** the Sun?
questions.fact: A year is about 365.25 days – that's why we have leap years.

questions.q: Which planet is called the **Morning Star**?
questions.fact: After the Moon, Venus is the brightest natural object in the night sky.

questions.q: Which planet has a giant **hexagon** storm?
questions.fact: Each side of the hexagon is wider than Earth.

questions.q: Which planet is **farthest** from the Sun?
questions.fact: Neptune is about 30 times farther from the Sun than Earth.

questions.q: Where is the main **asteroid belt**?
questions.fact: Asteroids in the belt are usually hundreds of thousands of km apart.

questions.q: What is the tallest **volcano** in the solar system?
questions.fact: Olympus Mons on Mars is about 22 km high.

questions.q: What is Saturn's **largest** moon?
questions.fact: Titan's thick atmosphere is mostly nitrogen, like Earth's.

questions.q: Which planet's **day** is closest to Earth's?
questions.fact: A day on Mars is called a sol.

questions.q: Which planet is the **coldest**?
questions.fact: Uranus has hit about −224 °C, the coldest planetary atmosphere.

questions.q: When did Pluto become a **dwarf planet**?
questions.fact: Pluto was discovered in 1930 by Clyde Tombaugh.

questions.q: Which planet was found by **maths** first?
questions.fact: Neptune was first seen in 1846 by Johann Galle.

questions.q: What is the largest object in the **asteroid belt**?
questions.fact: Ceres is about 940 km wide.

questions.q: Which moon is the most **volcanic**?
questions.fact: Io has around 400 active volcanoes.

questions.q: How many people have **walked** on the Moon?
questions.fact: The last Moon walk was in December 1972, on Apollo 17.

questions.q: How long is one **year** on Neptune?
questions.fact: Neptune finished its first orbit since discovery in 2011.

questions.q: What are the names of **Mars's** two moons?
questions.fact: Phobos orbits Mars three times a day.

questions.q: How hot is the Sun's **surface**?
questions.fact: The Sun's outer corona can top 1 million °C.

questions.q: What is the **farthest** human-made object?
questions.fact: Voyager 1 entered interstellar space in 2012.

questions.q: **Europa**, a moon with a hidden ocean, orbits…?
questions.fact: Europa's ocean may hold twice the water of Earth's oceans.

questions.q: How **old** is our solar system?
questions.fact: Earth's oldest known minerals are about 4.4 billion years old.

questions.q: What is the icy shell at our solar system's **edge**?
questions.fact: The Oort Cloud has never been seen directly.

questions.q: Which spacecraft flew past **Pluto** in 2015?
questions.fact: New Horizons took about 9.5 years to reach Pluto.

questions.q: Titan has **lakes**. What are they filled with?
questions.fact: Titan is the only other world with stable liquids on its surface.

questions.q: How many Earth days is a **year** on Mercury?
questions.fact: Mercury orbits the Sun at about 47 km per second.

questions.q: Who discovered Jupiter's four biggest **moons**?
questions.fact: They are still called the Galilean moons.

questions.q: Which planet has the most **volcanoes**?
questions.fact: Scientists have mapped about 85,000 volcanoes on Venus.
